answer: A single handclap releases a burst whose early reflections arrive at times fixed by the walls around it, and a device can prove its room by recording those reflection timings and comparing them with its registered pattern. The timings are a geometric signature of one specific space, so a farm would need a different real room per identity, and a guessed clap fails the timing test. The cipher of the first three reflections is hard to guess, a relic of an old plaster wall returns its own spacing, and a prism of echoes splits one clap into a code no other room shares.
